relationships.subject: CDK5
relationships.evidence_quote: CDK5 was observed to phosphorylate TRPV1 at T406, prompting the translocation of TRPV1 to the cell membrane and consequent augmentation of cellular excitability.

relationships.subject: CDK5
relationships.evidence_quote: The results demonstrated that CDK5 promoted TRPV1 membrane transport and neuron excitability through phosphorylation of TRPV1 at T406.

relationships.subject: CDK5
relationships.evidence_quote: Notably, CDK5 was found to directly bind to TRPV1, and the binding region was localized within the 1-390 amino acid sequence of TRPV1.

relationships.subject: miR-142-5p
relationships.evidence_quote: MiR-142-5p was shown to simultaneously bind to the mRNA of CDK5 and TRPV1, thereby inhibiting their expression.

relationships.subject: METTL14
relationships.evidence_quote: METTL14 could decelerate the maturation process of pri-miR-142 in an m6A-dependent manner, leading to a reduction in miR-142-5p expression.

relationships.subject: miR-142-5p
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal administration of miR-142-5p agomir exhibited therapeutic effects, while intrathecal administration of miR-142-5p antagomir induced inflammatory responses and hyperalgesia

key_findings: METTL14-mediated m6A modification of pri-miR-142 blocks its maturation, lowering miR-142-5p in DRG after CCI or LPS.
Reduced miR-142-5p de-represses CDK5 and TRPV1; CDK5 phosphorylates TRPV1 at T406 to drive membrane translocation and excitability.
